text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Government's new regional financing system costs 40 billion pesetas a year more than old one.
- Former spy Colonel Juan Alberto Perote offered to return missing military intelligence papers to Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) following the general election in March.
- Public sector unions unite against wage freeze.
- State attorney says vandalism in Basque country tripled in 1995.
EL MUNDO
- Government and unions seal pact on pensions until 2001.
- Unions tell public workers to boycott all non-essential consumer goods in protest against wage freeze.
- Michael Jackson, in Zaragoza for a concert, appeals to fans of all ages.
- A reserve fund worth 200 billion pesetas will guarantee new regional financing system does not create inequalities.
DIARIO 16
- Network for adopting Russia children fraudulently used Caritas seal.
- Former Socialist prime minister Felipe Gonzalez asks new Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar for more rigour.
ABC
- King Juan Carlos presides formal start of judicial year.
CINCO DIAS
- More taxes: government creates 10 new taxes and raises 10 more.
- Banco Central Hispano (BCH) mobilises branches to allocate shares among clients.
- Ikea, about to open a branch in Madrid, promises a year of fixed prices.
EXPANSION
- BCH will invest in Endesa and Retevision the 21 billion pesetas it earned from sale of Azucarera.
- Spain is on track to join a single European currency, according to The Economist.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Government promotes tax changes and accentuates budget control.
- Industry Ministry will replace Feliciano Fuster as chairman of Endesa as part of reform of electrical sector.
